mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strengthening labor market and rising consumer spending, which typically supports corporate earnings growth and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC for PAYEMS trend < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in rising PAYEMS periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 3.5%, it signals a tight labor market and strong economic growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate higher corporate profits.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in < 40% of instances when UNRATE < 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: The joint behavior of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) drives equity returns: when the Fed is cutting rates (FEDFUNDS decreasing) and inflation is rising (CPIAUCSL increasing), it signals a growth-oriented policy mix that boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS decreases and CPIAUCSL increases.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (defined by quarterly GDP growth above 2.0% and unemployment rate below 4.0%), the S&P 500 tends to underperform due to overvaluation and profit-taking, leading to negative 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances when the late-cycle expansion regime is active (GDPC1 growth > 2.0% and UNRATE < 4.0%).

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) indicates expanding manufacturing and services activity, which typically supports corporate earnings growth and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC for INDPRO trend < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 5-day forward returns in rising INDPRO periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 5.0%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that dampens economic growth and equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in < 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: The joint decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals a weakening consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as corporate revenue expectations are revised downward.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline.

mechanism_narrative: In a supply shock regime (defined by INDPRO declining > 1.0% and CPIAUCSL rising > 0.5% in the past month), the S&P 500 tends to underperform due to stagflationary pressures, leading to negative 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of instances when INDPRO declines > 1.0% and CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5%.
